Speech synthesis has evolved dramatically from concatenative unit selection systems to contemporary generative neural audio models. Today, flow-matching architectures, diffusion transformers, and autoregressive language models enable zero-shot voice cloning with remarkable timbre preservation and human-like naturalness. Despite these technical milestones, deploying frontier speech models on resource-constrained consumer hardware remains an intricate optimization challenge. Modern low-latency applications demand a delicate balance between acoustic fidelity, memory bandwidth, compute efficiency, and predictable time-to-first-audio. As research progresses toward unified speech foundation models, rigorous cross-architectural benchmarking provides essential empirical clarity for engineering teams.
